source_text: Quid ibi cognoscit diabolus suum, si nec quod factum, nec unde factum est, ipse condidit? ubi sit originale malum inter tot bona, unde sit in parvulis malum
pass_a_gloss: What there cognoscit the-devil his-own, if nor that/which made/done, nor whence made/done is, himself condidit? where may-be original evil among so-many goods, whence may-be in little-ones evil.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: Why is a human being whom God made under the devil?
What does the devil recognize there as his own, if he created neither what was made nor that from which it was made?
Among so many good things, where does the evil in infants come from?

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
